15.05.2023 REFERENCE PETITION UNDER SECTION 18 OF THE LAND ACQUISITION ACT 1894 AWARD:
Sh. Parmod S/O Late Sh. Anil Kumar vs Union Of India Through on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74758508/
1 (BY THE COURT U/S 26 OF LAND ACQUISITION ACT- 1894 ON REFERENCE PETITION U/S 18 OF THE ACT):
1. This reference under section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter called as LA Act), was sent to the reference court by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred as LAC).

2. As per the LAC Award, a large tract of land measuring 3078 bigha 14 biswa and 8 biswansi of village Khera Khurd, Delhi, was acquired by the Govt. for a public purpose namely "Rohini Residential Scheme, under Planned Development of Delhi".
Notification under Section 4 of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'LA Act') was issued on 21-03-2003.
Declaration under Section 6 was made on 19-03-2004.

Thereafter, Award bearing no.
05/2005-06/DC (NW) was announced by Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter LAC No.50/16 page 2 of 9 referred to as LAC) on 10-06-2005.
The LAC determined the market price of the acquired land as Rs.15,70,000/- per acre for land falling in Category 'A' and Rs.14,00,000/- per acre for land falling in 'B' Category.
3. The petitioner being dissatisfied with the market value determined by the LAC, filed the present petition u/s 18 of the LA Act, seeking reference to this court.
The Land Acquisition Collector forwarded the same to this court for adjudication.

4. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are that petitioner is/was the absolute owner/bhumidhar as well as in the cultivatory possession of the land bearing in khasra numbers as mentioned in the statement u/s 19 of the LA Act that was annexed with the present reference and admitted by the petitioner during the stage of admission/ denial of documents, situated within the Revenue Estate of Village Khera Khurd, Delhi (the said land).
The said land was acquired vide notification dated 21.03.2003.

The petitioner has preferred the present reference under section 18 of the Act essentially on the grievance that the market value of the acquired land has been erroneously determined at a low rate by the LAC so as to be LAC No.50/16 page 3 of 9 Rs.15,70,000/- per acre for land falling in Category 'A' and Rs.14,00,000/- per acre for land falling in 'B' Category.
5.

The petitioner has challenged the said award inter alia on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and incorrect assessment of market value of land inter-alia due to non-consideration of relevant factors like potentiality and fertility of the suit land, the surrounding colonies and developed areas, the market value of the adjoining areas/villages, the sale deeds of other lands of the contemporary period, nearness to the National Highway and industrial areas, the amenities available in the suit land etc.
6.
The petitioner has prayed compensation at enhanced rate besides interest thereon and solatium in addition to the compensation.

8.

The petition has been contested mainly on the ground that the LAC awarded adequate compensation to LAC No.50/16 page 4 of 9 the petitioner after taking into consideration all the relevant factors and therefore, LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land after taking into account the market rates prevailing at the time of notification under Section 4 of LA Act.
9. During the proceedings, the petitioner expired.
Consequently, application u/o 22 Rule 3 CPC was moved to implead his LRs i.e. 1.
Smt. Kanta Devi (wife), 2. Ms. Hemlata (daughter), 3.Ms. Kamlesh (daughter) and Sh. Parmod (son).
Vide order dated 14.11.2022 passed by the Undersigned, said application for impleadment of LRs of petitioner was allowed.
LRs mentioned in the application and SMC were same and impleaded.
Amended memo of parties was also filed.

During the proceedings LRs namely 1.Smt. Kanta Devi (wife), 2.Ms. Hemlata (daughter) and 3.Ms.
Kamlesh (daughter) had relinquished their right vide relinquishment deed, in favour of Sh. Parmod (son), vide order dated 17.03.2023.
10.
During admission-denial of documents, the counsel for petitioner admitted the statement given u/s 19 of the Act.

The following issues were framed :-
LAC No.50/16 page 5 of 9 1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?

2. Relief.
11.
In evidence, the petitioner has relied upon the judgment in a case Prem Chand vs. UOI and also the evidence led in said case.
12. The respondent no.2/ Delhi Development Authority (DDA) in its evidence, tendered the award as Ex. R1.
The respondent no. 1/Union of India (UOI) did not lead the evidence.
13. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have also carefully considered the record.

My issue-wise findings are given as under:-
FINDINGS ON ISSUE NO. 1 :-
14.
Petitioner has contended that valuation of land determined by LAC is not reasonable as LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.
However, he has not led any evidence to show as to how the LAC was wrong in fixing market value of land.

petitioner has relied only upon the judgment titled as Prem Chand Vs. UOI in LAC No.1529/16 vide judgement dated 01.09.2018 decided LAC No.50/16 page 6 of 9 by Sh. Neeraj Gaur, Ld. ADJ-01,
Delhi, Ld. Predecessor of this Court and conceded that award be passed in terms of the said judgment and the same enhancement which was granted in the said judgment be also granted to petitioner.

entities.text: Prem Chand Vs. UOI in LAC No.1529/16
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
15. In Prem Chand case (supra), ld. Predecessor has determined the market value of the land of village Khera Khurd that was acquired vide same notification dated 21.03.2003 as Rs.19,80,750/-
per acre.
There is nothing on record to infer that the petitioner's land was not at par with the land involved in Prem chand's case (supra).
On the strength of the discussion made in Prem Chand's case, I have to arrive at the same conclusion and determine the same market value as was determined therein.
16. Petitioner has also claimed compensation for crops, tree, tubewell etc.
However, the petitioner has failed to lead any evidence to substantiate his claim or to establish that he was not awarded sufficient compensation for same.
Accordingly, I hold that petitioner is not entitled to any enhancement in compensation on this count.

17. Besides above, petitioner shall be entitled to other LAC No.50/16 page 7 of 9 statutory benefits under the LA Act viz. 12% additional amount [as per section 23 (1A)] and 30% solatium [u/s 23 (2)]
and will be entitled to interest under Section 28 of L.A Act on the fair market value @ 9% per annum for the first year and @ 15% for subsequent year till the making of payment of enhanced compensation by LAC as per provision of Section 28 of the Act.
Issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.

18. Findings on Issue No.2 - RELIEF
In view of the findings on Issue no.1, the petitioner/s are granted the following reliefs: -
i. fair market value @ Rs.19,80,750/- per acre, for the acquired land as per statement u/s 19 of the L.A. Act thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,10,750/- per acre;

iii. solatium u/s 23(2) of LA Act @ 30% on the enhanced amount of market value;
LAC No.50/16 page 8 of 9 iv. interest under Section 28 of L.A Act @ 9% per annum for the first year from the date of dispossession and at the rate of 15% per annum on the difference between the enhanced compensation awarded by this court and the compensation awarded by the LAC for the subsequent period till its payment.
Sh. Parmod S/O
The share(s) of the petitioner(s) would be determinable as per the statement u/s 19 of the L.A.
Act proved on record and the said statement shall constitute a part of this award.
20. Reference petition stands answered.
